newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Improved signs for steel in western Europe - IISI.
newsitem.headline: Improved signs for steel in western Europe - IISI.

text.p: World crude steel production was unchanged at 59.6 million tonnes in August compared with the same month last year, the International Iron and Steel Institute (IISI) said on Monday.
However, IISI said output during the first eight months of the year was 1.7 percent below the level in the same 1995 period.
On a positive note, it said the results of the August survey showed the first signs of slowing decline in western Europe and that production continued to grow in North America.
"In western Europe stocks are finally coming into line with actual demand," IISI said in a statement.
British production rose 6.4 percent to 1.4 million tons in August compared with the same month last year while output in Italy, France, Spain and Belgium remained below the 1995 level.
For all of western Europe, production still fell 3.4 percent to 12.4 million tons in August.
In rump Yugoslavia, Serbia and Montenegro, output soared 389.4 percent to sixty-nine thousand tons.
In eastern Europe, output fell 14.0 percent to 2.6 million tons, partly because of lower exports to the west.
But in former Soviet Union, output fell only 1.4 percent.

"This indicated relative stability in Russia and Ukraine - even though Russian output remained below the 1995 level due to less profitable exports since the imposition of the 'rouble corridor'," IISI said.

Production in North America firmed slightly to 10 million tons, despite some production problems, and rose 3.2 percent in South America to 3.2 million tons. African output fell by 6.7 percent while it rose 24.2 percent in the Middle East.
"Asia's steel producing nations continue to have crude steel outputs well above year-erlier results -- with positive signs also for Japan's production," IISI said.
Chinese output jumped 6.6 percent to 8.3 million tons.
